subject: Intermittent request failures: suspected transit inspection
messages:
From: Adam Chen <adam.chen@lyra.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: network-admin@lyra.ai
Date: Thu, 11 May 2028 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: High error rate + latency from Lyra -> Redwood (prod)

Hi Neha,

We started seeing a jump in 5xx responses and tail latency from our production traffic to Redwood endpoints around 07:50 UTC this morning. Impact is ~12% of requests with spikes to 28s for some customer-facing operations. Our SRE stack shows a simultaneous increase in TCP retransmits between our GCP VPC and Redwood's ingress IPs.

Attached is a short p95 trace dump and a pcap excerpt from the Lyra side. We’re trying to rule out application regressions but the network team is seeing packet-level anomalies (retransmits and timeouts) before the requests reach your edge. Can you confirm if there were any routing changes, maintenance, or security policy updates on your side?

We’re sensitive to this — are you able to spin up a direct alternate route or bypass any inline inspection while we triage?

Thanks,
Adam
Adam Chen
Platform Lead, Lyra AI
Adam.Chen@lyra.ai

Attachments: lyra_p95_traces_20280511.txt; packet_capture_excerpt.pcap

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Adam Chen <adam.chen@lyra.ai>, network-admin@lyra.ai
Date: Thu, 11 May 2028 09:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High error rate + latency from Lyra -> Redwood (prod)

Neha / Adam — quick triage update from infra: we’re seeing an uptick in TCP retransmits and RTT variance on flows originating from the GCP region used by Lyra to our SFO POP between 07:45–08:10 UTC. Key observations: 

- Flow logs show a sequence of SYN/ACK delays and duplicate ACKs that align with the customer pcap.
- The packet samples indicate an inline device re-ordering or buffering large TLS records; this pattern is consistent with deep packet inspection (DPI) appliances or an HTTP proxy performing connection-level buffering under load.
- No config changes were pushed from Redwood in the last 24 hours to the SFO edge. However, cloud provider routing (transit) shows a transient reroute through a third-party transit hop (AS64523) between 07:40–08:05 UTC.

Actions taken: 
1) Collected flowlogs slice and a 60s pcap excerpt (attached).
2) Temporarily increased TCP keepalive and lowered our TLS record size tuning for flows from the Lyra CIDRs to reduce head-of-line stalls.
3) Opening a ticket with the cloud provider (Marta Lopez cc'd) to verify whether the transit hop performed inline inspection or path MTU manipulation.

Suggested mitigation (short window): if Lyra can route traffic to our ORD POP (alternate POP) or allow our IPs to bypass their HTTP inspection for a 30–60 minute triage window, we can validate if the inline hop is the cause.

Attaching: packet_capture_excerpt.pcap; flowlogs_slice_08-11-2028.tar.gz

— Jonas Weber
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Jonas — thanks for the quick deep-dive and attachments. We ran the packet capture through our appliances and can reproduce the retransmit pattern you noted. Our team also confirmed a short-lived route change in GCP that pushed traffic through a transit partner that applies TLS/MITM inspection for some peered paths (this was unexpected).

We’ll temporarily permit direct routing to your ORD POP and add a bypass rule for the Redwood destination IPs so you can validate. Can you also advise whether Redwood can provision an alternate hostname for Lyra that maps to ORD to avoid DNS-level stickiness?

Adam
Adam Chen
Platform Lead, Lyra AI

Thanks team — appreciate the rapid work. I approve a customer goodwill credit (one week of committed capacity rebate) and priority remediation. Please confirm the following by EOD:

- Jonas: Will the ORD routing test remove the failure mode? If yes, schedule the ORD cut and notify Lyra with an ETA.
- Rishi: If the ORD bypass fixes the issue, prepare a permanent routing/fallback policy so Lyra traffic prefers alternate POPs when transit metrics degrade.
- Neha/Grace: Coordinate credit and contract note with Sales Ops/Finance; include a short executive summary for Lyra.

Keep me posted; escalate if anything looks like a larger systemic transit problem across customers.
